column2: bearing in the right hand and in the left a bell and a shield, a skull-staff and a trident — called Siddha-Chamunda,
the goddess Siddhayogeshvari, giver of all accomplishments. Another may be of this form, red, with noose and goad,
Bhairavi, Rupavidya, with twelve arms. These are born in cremation grounds, fierce; this is remembered as the group of eight mothers.
Kshama, covered with jackals, old, two-armed, open-mouthed, toothy, beneficent, standing on the ground with hands on knees.
Yakshinis have fixed long eyes; Shakinis crooked glances; Apsarases are tawny-eyed, very lovely, always beautiful.
Nandisha the door-guard with rosary and trident; Mahakala with sword and skull, with spear and shield;
thin, with bent limbs, dancing; Kushmanda stout and dwarfish; elephant-faced, cow-eared and the like, the hosts led by Virabhadra.
Ghantakarna with eighteen arms, tearing sin and disease: thunderbolt, sword, staff, discus, arrow, pestle, goad and club;
on the right a forefinger, shield, spear, skull and noose; bow, bell, axe, and with two a trident; the god covered with a garland of bells, crusher of boils.
Chandra, Chandravali, Prapancha, Pralayantika, Shishuvaktra, Pishachi and the greedy Pishitasha;
Dhamani, Tapani, Ragini, Vikritanana; Vayuvega, Brihatkukshi, Vikrita, Vishvarupika;
Yamajihva, Jayanti, Durjaya, Jayantika; Vidali, Revati, Putana, Vijayantika;
eight-handed or four-handed, wielding wished weapons, giving all accomplishments. Bhairava should have sun-hands, a bent-elbow face, bearing matted hair and moon;
with sword, goad, axe and arrow on one side, bearing fear for all; bow, trident, skull-staff and noose, and a half-boon raised;
wearing an elephant hide with two, adorned with a skin garment and serpent; corpse-eating, to be worshipped among the mothers, or five-faced.
In reverse order up to fire, divided by the long eight and one; with its six limbs and the endings of the classes, one should worship in order.
Mounted on the temple and fire-petal, with gold and mercury, joined with nada, bindu and drop, lit by the lord of the mothers and limbs.
Virabhadra mounted on a bull, in front of the mothers, four-faced; Gauri two-armed, three-eyed, with trident, mirror,
trident, rosary, pot, boon-giving, four-armed; on a lotus, Lalita; with the Skanda host's rod of mirror,
Chandika with hand, bearing sword, trident, spear; on right and left serpent-noose, shield, goad and axe; bow; on a lion, a buffalo struck in front by the trident.
One may take the make by banners and the like, by gods, elements or fires; those fingers, the remainder, one should mark as auspicious or inauspicious.
Banner and the like — banner, lion, elephant, bull — the first are best, the others auspicious; among notes Shadja, Gandhara and Panchama give good.
Among elements the earth is good; the Ahavaniya among fires. In half the stated length divided in order by the serpent-parts,
by six, by element-parts, by a sixth, by a third, and by five more; it is square for the wealthy, the poor, Brihaspati, and the sun alike.
The fifth is called Vardhamana, from increase of girth over breadth. There are two kinds; many are to be told here from Vishvakarman.
Of the wealthy and others there are three kinds by stoutness; that shaken-off, eightfold; threefold by hand is called Jina, joined with all alike.
Twenty-five lingas — not in the first, worshipped by gods likewise; five and seven by unity, with devotees of Jinas.
Fourteen thousand and fourteen hundred; thus the breadth eight fingers, from nine and one cubit within.
By the corner and half-corner parts of those one should think the corners by cords; making the breadth middling, or three should be set in the middle.
Above the division it is eight-cornered; sixteen-cornered is the Shiva part; from the foot to the knee is Brahma; to the navel Vishnu;
to the head the lord of elements, in the manifest and unmanifest of it. In the arrangement of five lingas the head is called round.
Umbrella-like or cock-like, or of the form of a crescent moon. By fourfold division of each, I shall tell the fruit by difference of desire.
One should make the width of the linga's head divided by eight; one should divide the first part fourfold by breadth and height.
Four lines there by dropping part by part; the Pundarika by one part; the Vishala by erasing;
the Shrivatsa by cutting three; the Shatrukrit by erasing four; the head in the all-equal is best; the cock-like in the Suraha.
In the linga of four parts, the Trapusha by erasing two; the head of the beginningless is declared; hear the half-moon head.
By a part at the end, by four parts, one-day, nectar-eyed; the full young moon, kumuda, by two, three, four, in decreasing order.
Four, three, one-faced — hear then the face-linga. The worship portion should be made, arranged by form, fire and foot.
Having left aside the sun-part as before, one should turn six places: the head height should be made, the forehead, nose,
mouth, chin, neck, by parts of four, with arms and eyes; having folded with the hands according to the measure of the image.
The face should be made equal toward each, by an eighth of the breadth. The four-faced I have told; hear the three-faced.
It has ear-feet extra; forehead and the like one should indicate. The arms should be made by four parts; the west is strong.
By an eighth of the breadth is the projection of the faces. One-faced should be made in the east with gentle eyes.
One should project the forehead, nose, mouth and neck; from the arm by a fifth part, one should project armless.
By a sixth of the breadth the projection of the faces is good. For all face-lingas, the Trapusha or the cock.
Pots should be set in the east and elsewhere, and four pots should be set at the corners of the altar with the "Ajighra" mantra.
Having invoked Indra and the others into the pots, one should worship in order in the east and so on: "Come, Indra, king of gods, thunderbolt-handed, seated on an elephant;
protect my east door with the gods; homage to you." Having worshipped with the mantra "Savior Indra," the wise one should sacrifice.
Come in front, with Shakti, seated on a goat, with strength; protect the southeast direction with the gods; accept worship; homage to you.
With the mantra "Agni-murdha" one should worship; "Homage to Agni." "Come, Yama, seated on a buffalo, staff in hand, mighty;
protect the south door, Vaivasvata; homage to you." One should worship Yama with "Vaivasvata Sangamana."
Come, Nirrita, rich in sword, with strength and vehicle; this arghya, this foot-water; protect the Nirrita direction.
This is for you, Nirrita — the man should worship with this mantra with arghya and the rest. "Varuna, mounted on a crocodile, noose in hand, mighty,
come; protect the west door, protect; homage to you." The teacher should worship Varuna with "Uruḥ hi raja" with arghya and the rest.
Come, Vayu, strong, banner in hand, with vehicle; protect the northwest with the gods and Maruts; homage to you.
With "Vata" and the rest, or "homage to Vayu." "Come, Soma, strong, mace in hand, with vehicle;
protect the north door, with Kubera; homage to you." Or "Soma the king"; "homage to Soma."
Come, Ishana, strong, trident in hand, seated on a bull; protect the northeast direction of the sacrificial pavilion; homage to you.
One should worship with "Ishanam asya," or "homage to Ishana." "Brahma, come, seated on a swan, with ladles in hand,
protect the upper direction with the worlds, unborn of the sacrifice; homage to you." One should worship with "Hiranyagarbha"; "homage to Brahma."

Come, Ananta, rich in discus, seated on the tortoise, lord of the serpent host; protect, protect the lower direction, lord of Ananta; homage to you. One should worship with "Namo astu sarpa"; "homage to Ananta."
Some should place pots with soil from sacred places and mountains; some nagakesara flowers and saffron.
Others should place sandal, agaru and camphor and flowers; lapis lazuli, coral, pearl, crystal and diamond.
Having put these together in one place, establish it, best of gods. Another should be placed with waters of rivers, great rivers and lakes.
Other pots should be placed in the pavilion at eighty-one places, filled with scented water and the like, consecrated with the Shri-sukta.
Barley, mustard seed, scent, kusha tips and rice, likewise sesame, fruit and flowers for arghya should be placed in the east.
Lotus, shyamalata, durva, Vishnuparni and kusha for foot-water on the right side; honey-mixture on the right.
Kakkola, clove and auspicious nutmeg; in the north for rinsing; in the fire a vessel with durva and rice;
a vessel for the lamp-waving and for the rubbing in the wind; a vessel with scent and flowers in the northeast placed in a vessel.
Mura, mamsi, amalaka, sahadeva, and turmeric and the rest; one should place sixty lamps, eight for the lamp-waving.
Conch, discus, Shrivatsa, thunderbolt, lotus and the rest, having made them in a golden vessel, with flowers of various colors.
As in the god so in the body one should apply the principles. On the discus-lotus mandala one should likewise worship Vishnu with scent and the rest.
As before one should meditate on the seat with limbs and retinue; above one should contemplate the auspicious twelve-spoked wheel,
a wheel with three hubs and two rims, joined with the vowels. Then the wise one should place on the back Prakriti and the rest.
One should worship the sun twelvefold again on the tips of the spokes; there one should contemplate the moon joined with sixteen digits.
